page.layout: One page of text. At the top, a running title in small capitals (EMBLEMA) above a large Greek title and its second line, centred. Below them a woodcut emblem, centred. Below the woodcut, four centred lines of italic verse. At the lower right, the catchword.

main_text.head: EMBLEMA ΜΗΤ' ἈΝΤΙΓΝΩΕΙΝ ἈΝΕΜΟΙΣΙΝ.
main_text.p: [woodcut emblem: a globe-shaped ship's hull with a column topped by a cockerel, two banners reading FIDES and IVSTITIA, a sun, a town on a hill, and a winged figure at a steering oar in rough sea]

l.i: Atq; malos noris seculi adesse dies.
Ut refles ventis, caueas, polypiq; teneto
Mentem, qui quœuis saxa colore refert.

page.notes: The Greek title is set in capitals and was read from the scan; the letters ΜΗΤ' and ΑΝΤΙΓΝΩΕΙΝ are not fully certain, so the second word may need checking against the original. The page number at top left is a stylised numeral and is read here as 78 [?]. The word "refles" in line three is uncertain [?]. A small reference-type sign follows "memento," at the end of line one; it has no matching note. The woodcut is described, not transcribed. The catchword "Naui-" is a hyphenated word beginning the next page.
